findings.text: non-blocking: the contract is stamped only by the batch entry queue_requests, which has no production caller (grep over reckon/ finds dispatch.py:287 defines the delegate and nothing invokes it); production queue writes go through runs.queue_dispatch, which stamps nothing, so every production pointer falls to _dispatch_gate_owed and behaves exactly as before this node. The narrowed hold is therefore inert in production until the coordinator's separate wiring node lands; the node names this in its fragment and its outside_scope, so it is declared rather than hidden.

non-blocking: the landing record states the pending production wiring plainly but omits the second unmet done_when item — that routing._document_change_is_contract still resolves review_run_id, review_report_directory and _REVIEW_SNAPSHOT_NAME itself instead of reading the snapshot through plan_review._snapshot_evidence. The manifest records it under blockers and outside_scope, but the fragment becomes the plan comment, so plan section 10 will read as fully satisfied while one carried requirement is not.
